content.value_statement: Background jobs often fail when queues, retries, and long waits are managed by hand. This skill guides durable Inngest workflows with typed events, retries, sleeps, and deployment checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains Inngest function setup for Next.js serve handlers and typed events.
Models multi-step jobs with step.run, sleeps, retries, and concurrency limits.
Shows fan-out patterns for orders, digests, webhook handling, and AI processing.
Defines validation checks for serve handlers, function IDs, step names, timeouts, and idempotency.
Maps related tasks to supporting skills for queues, databases, deployment, and email systems.
Clarifies when Inngest fits serverless background jobs and event-driven workflows.
limitations: It does not manage Redis queue infrastructure or Temporal workflows.
It does not replace production testing, monitoring, or provider documentation.
It assumes users already have an application framework and service credentials.
It provides guidance only; it does not run deployments or create accounts.

use_cases.title: Launch Background Jobs
use_cases.description: Create serverless jobs for welcome emails, delayed follow-ups, daily digests, and routine cleanup tasks.

use_cases.title: Process Webhooks Safely
use_cases.description: Design webhook workflows with idempotency, retries, and durable steps for payments and subscriptions.

use_cases.title: Automate AI Pipelines
use_cases.description: Break long AI processing into reliable steps with concurrency limits and recoverable checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add my first Inngest function to a Next.js app. Include typed events, the serve handler, and one durable step.

prompt_templates.title: Add Durable Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Inngest workflow for an order process with inventory checks, payment, fulfillment, retries, and concurrency limits.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Webhook Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my webhook flow for Inngest. Recommend idempotency keys, retry settings, event names, and safe failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Inngest architecture for serve registration, step naming, timeouts, fan-out, concurrency, deployment limits, and observability gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a welcome email job after user signup.
output: Recommends a typed signup event and a welcome email function.
Adds a durable wait before a follow-up tips email.
Checks that the serve handler registers the function.

output_examples.input: I need reliable Stripe webhook processing.
output: Suggests sending webhook events into Inngest with a Stripe event idempotency key.
Separates payment logic into named durable steps.
Adds retry and failure guidance for downstream services.

output_examples.input: My AI document job takes several minutes.
output: Splits extraction, chunking, embedding, and storage into checkpoints.
Recommends concurrency limits for model and vector database calls.
Flags retry and timeout decisions for production review.

best_practices: Use descriptive step names and keep each step idempotent.
Set concurrency limits for APIs, payments, emails, and other constrained services.
Add idempotency keys for payment and webhook workflows.
anti_patterns: Using Inngest for Redis queue management when BullMQ fits better.
Waiting for events without a timeout.
Putting long external calls outside durable steps.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Inngest functions, event workflows, scheduled jobs, webhook processors, and durable AI pipelines.

faq.question: Does it replace Inngest documentation?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance, but provider documentation and production testing remain necessary.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for Inngest clients, functions, and serve handlers in Next.js.

faq.question: Does it manage queue infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Inngest workflows, not Redis, BullMQ, or worker infrastructure management.

faq.question: How does it improve reliability?
faq.answer: It emphasizes durable steps, retries, sleeps, idempotency, timeouts, and concurrency controls.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
